title: A quota balances only what it counts
statement: A quota balances only the level it counts, so set and check targets for the standards and formats inside each domain, not only for the domains.
example: One adaptive test came within one item of its domain quotas in every simulated session while its bank held 28 items on one standard against a target of 8.
detail: A reading assessment's simulation held its domain quotas to within one item in 100% of sessions, and its write-up says this does not guarantee balance across the standards inside a domain, which bank composition and the item-selection rule decide (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`). Its bank held 28 items on one third-grade standard and 19 on another, each against a target of 8, and 31 on a third, 26 of them on prefix meaning (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/reference/CAT_MAP_EXAM_SPEC.md`). Two formats were stocked above their per-form targets as well, so they will be seen more often than intended even though the engine enforces per-session quotas. A cap of two items per standard per session was proposed, not shipped.
against: A topic cap limits how often any one topic appears in a session, which the package counts as some mitigation (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md`, line 268), and the over-testing is its expectation, not a measured serving rate. The per-standard counts come from a matrix the same file marks as stale, though it undercounted rather than overcounted (lines 121–132).

evidence.quote: Blueprint adherence at the domain level does not guarantee standard-level balance.
the distribution across RL standards is determined by bank composition and Fisher-information selection
Domain quota enforcement verified across 1,000 simulated sessions.
Three G3 standards are over-represented: RL.3.3 (28 items vs. target 8), RI.3.3 (19 items vs. target 8), and L.3.4 (31 items with 26 marked deprioritized).
A per-standard session cap (max 2 items per standard per session) is proposed

The bank's MSQ and hot-text counts are above the per-form targets. This does not block delivery — the CAT enforces per-session quotas — but means these formats will be seen more frequently than intended before additional MCQ/EBSR items are added.
- L.3.4 is over-concentrated on prefix meaning specifically (26 of 31 items)
